calibration.reference_design: bitset subset-sum DP construction (invoices smallest-first, exact reconstruction via the classic value-domain bitset trick) followed by simulated annealing with a FIXED iteration count (15000) and FIXED restart count (25) per customer -- not wall-clock-time-based. Confirmed byte-for-byte identical output across two consecutive match() calls with the same inputs, completing both calls in ~47s combined, well inside the 140s budget.
calibration.note: A real reviewer found that a much simpler combination -- the same bitset subset-sum DP seed (a substantially better construction than best-fit-decreasing greedy), followed by a plain first-improvement hill climb with no annealing and no restarts (20k iterations) -- reached 3.53%-3.66% of total value on the held-out scenario (we reproduced their approach and measured 928,781 cents / 3.66%, close to their reported figure), which cleared the PREVIOUS bar (1,250,000 cents). This was a genuine, useful finding: the DP seed is a real improvement over best-fit-decreasing that our own reference had not been using. We adopted the DP seed into the reference itself and combined it with the existing annealing+restarts search, reaching 810,433 cents (3.19%) -- swept across 5 independently generated scenarios, the annealing-refined reference beats the DP-seed-plus-plain-hill-climb probe by 22.5%-37.5% relative cost on every one, with zero exceptions. The pass bar sits between the DP-seed-plus-hill-climb probe (928,781) and the full reference (810,433), close to the reference side.
